To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tobacco industry and its associates lobbied to have the definition of tobacco addiction narrowed in the DSM-III, that the industry and its allies worked to mitigate the impact of the inclusion of tobacco addiction in the DSM-3 following its publication, and that these efforts mirror industry tactics to undermine the spread of a scientific and public understanding of the health effects of tobacco that would reduce smoking and tobacco industry profits.
the American Psychiatric Associations (APA) definition of tobacco dependence and its inclusion in DSM III was influenced by the tobacco industry.

the tobacco industry and its allied psychiatrists lobbied to limit the scope of tobacco dependence in the DSM-III, that the tobacco industry worked to minimise the impact of the publication of DSM-iii, and that the tobacco industry’s actions to influence the DSM were part of a pattern of industry actions to influence health research and policy in a way that would protect its profits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the tobacco industry on the American Psychiatric Associations definition of tobacco related mental disorders.
the role of the tobacco industry in influencing the definition of nicotine dependence in DSM-III.
the influence of the tobacco industry in the development of diagnostic criteria for tobacco dependence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tobacco industry has been involved in a long-term, systematic, and well-organised campaign to influence the definition of smoking and tobacco use disorders in the DSM-III, DSM-III-R, and DSM-IV.
the tobacco industry and its associates lobbied the APA to narrow the definition and impact of tobacco dependence and to try to limit its effects after its publication.
the tobacco companies and their allies worked to narrow the definition, and to limit the impact of the DSM-3 definition of tobacco dependence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tobacco industry has been working to influence the content and impact of the DSM for many years.
the tobacco industry has a long history of trying to influence psychiatric research, including the DSM.
tobacco companies have a history of working with the APA to influence the definition of smoking and health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tobacco industry and its sympathisers have been and are likely to continue to be active in influencing psychiatric and public health policy.

tobacco industry tactics to influence the definition of tobacco addiction in the DSM-III are part of a pattern of industry influence on public health policy that has been documented in many countries.
the tobacco industry has been and continues to be a formidable adversary in the struggle for tobacco control.
